'''Jesé Rodríguez Ruiz''' ({{IPA|es|xeˈse roˈðɾiɣeθ ˈrwiθ}}; born 26 February 1993) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as [[Winger (football)|winger]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Segunda División]] club [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]].

An academy graduate of [[La Liga]] side [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], Jesé debuted for the senior team in 2011, making 94 appearances across all competitions for the club and scoring eighteen goals. During his time in Madrid, which was disrupted by a serious knee injury in 2014, he won two [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] medals, as well as a title in each of La Liga, the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] and the [[Copa del Rey]].

Jesé left the club in 2016 to join [[Ligue 1]] side [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] for a reported fee of €25 million, before returning to Spain six months later to join hometown club Las Palmas on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] for the remainder of the season. Jesé then joined [[Premier League]] side [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on loan for the [[2017–18 Stoke City F.C. season|2017–18 season]], and later [[Real Betis]] for the second half of the [[2018–19 La Liga|2018–19 La Liga campaign]]. After a brief loan spell with [[Primeira Liga]] club [[Sporting CP]], Jesé left PSG to rejoin Las Palmas on a permanent deal.

On the international stage, Jesé earned 36 caps at youth level for Spain from [[Spain national under-16 football team|under-16]] to [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21]] level, scoring sixteen goals overall. He was part of the [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain U19]] side which won the [[2012 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] and claimed the Golden Boot award for ending as the tournament's top goalscorer.<ref name=int>{{cite web|url=http://www.sbnews.co.za/2014/02/jese-rodriguez-player-profile.html|title=Player Profile: Jese Rodriguez|website=Soccer Betting News|date=February 2014|access-date=7 January 2017|archive-date=8 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170108191048/http://www.sbnews.co.za/2014/02/jese-rodriguez-player-profile.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jesé is also a [[musician]] and goes by the stage name Jey M. He was previously part of a two-man [[reggaeton]] band which was formed in March 2014 and disbanded later that year.

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
====Early career====
Born in [[Las Palmas]], [[Canary Islands]], Jesé began his football career with local team [[AD Huracán|Huracán]] in 2005, whom he joined from amateur side El Pilar.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsportsasia.com/en-ph/news/las-palmas-could-miss-out-on-jese/|title=Las Palmas could miss out on Jese|website=Fox Sport|date=28 December 2016|access-date=2 January 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103005753/http://www.foxsportsasia.com/en-ph/news/las-palmas-could-miss-out-on-jese/|archive-date=3 January 2017}}</ref> His form at youth level for the club saw him attract interest from [[La Liga]] sides [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], but he opted to sign for [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]'s [[La Fábrica (Real Madrid)|youth system]] in 2007, aged 14.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.canarias7.es/articulo.cfm?id=195640|title=Jesé Rodríguez, la perla del Madrid (Jesé Rodríguez, Madrid's pearl)|website=Canarias7|date=28 December 2010|language=es|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=3 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303165759/http://www.canarias7.es/articulo.cfm?id=195640|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=FCB>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadridnews.com/barcelona-tried-sign-jese-rodriguez-6194|title=When Barcelona tried to sign Jese Rodriguez|website=Real Madrid News|date=24 December 2013|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=20 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820215140/http://www.realmadridnews.com/barcelona-tried-sign-jese-rodriguez-6194|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé made his senior debut for the [[Real Madrid Castilla]] side on 16 January 2011 in a 5–0 [[Segunda División B]] home win over [[Universidad de Las Palmas CF|Universidad de Las Palmas]]. His performance throughout the match, which included an assist for [[Dani Carvajal]], drew early comparisons to fellow Real Madrid teammate and multiple [[Ballon d'Or]] winner, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/01/16/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1295198191.html|title=Jesé debuta en el Castilla con un detalle a lo Ronaldo (Jesé makes debut with Castilla with Ronaldo-like detail)|website=Marca|date=16 January 2011|language=es|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=10 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110610094949/http://www.marca.com/2011/01/16/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1295198191.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé spent most of the season with Real Madrid's ''Juvenil A'' team, however, and enjoyed a successful 2010–11 campaign which earned him a permanent promotion to the Castilla side.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/03/01/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1299006770.html|title=El Madrid ata a Jesé Rodríguez|trans-title=Madrid ties Jesé Rodríguez|website=Marca|date=1 March 2011|language=es|access-date=4 June 2013|archive-date=29 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029205344/http://www.marca.com/2011/03/01/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1299006770.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2011–13: Youth and entrance to the first team squad====

In July 2011, Jesé was selected by first-team [[Manager (association football)|manager]] [[José Mourinho]] for the club's pre-season tour of the United States and made his non-competitive debut for Real Madrid in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Los Angeles Galaxy]], coming on as a 64th minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[José Callejón]] and scoring in a 5–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ronaldo7.net/news/2012/532-la-galaxy-1-5-real-madrid-opening-the-tour-with-a-classic-manita.html|title=LA Galaxy 1–5 Real Madrid: Opening the tour with a classic manita|website=Ronaldo 7|date=2 August 2011|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=20 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120232252/http://www.ronaldo7.net/news/2012/532-la-galaxy-1-5-real-madrid-opening-the-tour-with-a-classic-manita.html|url-status=usurped}}</ref> He returned to the Castilla for the start of the season and scored his first goal on 2 October 2011 against [[La Roda CF|La Roda]], finishing an [[Assist (football)|assist]] from [[Álvaro Morata]] in a 4–2 away loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/10/02/spain/segunda-b/la-roda-cf/real-madrid-castilla-club-de-futbol/1162345/|title=La Roda v Real Madrid II 4–2|website=Soccerway|date=2 October 2011|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=25 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225075756/http://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/10/02/spain/segunda-b/la-roda-cf/real-madrid-castilla-club-de-futbol/1162345/|url-status=live}}</ref> Having impressed with the reserve side during the first half of the season, Jesé was handed his senior debut on 12 December in [[2011–12 Copa del Rey|the first round]] of the [[Copa del Rey]], replacing Ronaldo for the final fifteen minutes of a 2–0 away triumph over [[SD Ponferradina]]. After the match Jesé dedicated his debut to his family who had supported him in fulfilling his dream.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2011/12/13/mas_futbol/1323730856_850215.html|title=Callejón brilla y Jesé debuta|website=AS|last=Garcia|first=Oscar|date=13 December 2011|language=es|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=4 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804183348/https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2011/12/13/mas_futbol/1323730856_850215.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/12/14/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1323818247.html|title=Jesé, un sueño cumplido (Jesé, fulfilled dream)]|website=Marca|last=Polo|first=Pablo|date=13 December The following season, after criticism that players from the Castilla were not being given a fair chance, Mourinho stated that it was difficult to do so as the senior side played a different style to the reserves. He also highlighted the position Jesé was being played in as one that did not exist in the main squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1208403/jose-mourinho-questions-real-madrid%27s-youth-system?cc=5739|title=Jose Mourinho questions Real Madrid's youth system|website=ESPN FC|last=Delaney|first=Miguel|date=31 October 2012|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=31 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231220042/http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1208403/jose-mourinho-questions-real-madrid%27s-youth-system?cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé's lack of opportunity prompted agent Ginés Carvajal
to publicly state that they would need to study options for the player's future if he was not permanently promoted to the first team the following year with the guarantee he would receive more playing time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/12/29/en/football/real_madrid/1356813486.html|title=Jesé wants Mou to give him a chance|website=Marca|date=29 December 2012|access-date=25 January 2013, in an interview with ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'', Jesé spoke out against his lack of senior game, stating that he was confident he was doing well enough to be granted an opportunity and, while he tried to learn as much as he could from Mourinho, he was a manager who surrounded himself with players who had already made their name.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/02/20/en/football/real_madrid/1361344773.html|title=Jesé: "I don't understand why they don't give me an opportunity"|last=Cerezo|first=Hugo|website=Marca|date=20 web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story?id=1346912&cc=5739|title=Lack of Real chances may force Jese exit|website=ESPN FC|last=Corrigan|first=Dermot|date=20 February 2013|access-date=20 April }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/02/25/en/football/real_madrid/1361778430.html|title=Jesé's back-up|website=Marca|first=J.I.|last=Garcia-Ochoa|date=25 February In spite of his struggles in breaking into the first-team, Jesé continued to excel for the Castilla and on 2 June he broke the record for most goals scored in a single season for the reserve side, netting a solo goal in a 4–0 home win over [[AD Alcorcón]] to surpass the record of 21 goals set by [[Emilio Butragueño]] in [[1983–84 Segunda División|1983–84]].<ref>{{cite who described him as the jewel in the crown of ''Los Blancos''' academy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/06/03/en/football/real_madrid/1370249450.html|title=Jesé: the Galáctico on Real's
