====2013–16: Rising influence, injury and decline====
While at the [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] with Spain, Jesé was the subject of mass media speculation that he could be leaving Real Madrid following his lack of game-time with the first team the season before. The club's technical director, [[Miguel Pardeza]], categorically stated on 13 July that the player would remain at the club, however, and Jesé extended his contract for a further four years later in the same month, signing a deal worth more than €1 million a year and which contained a €200 million release clause.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11675/8824111/Transfer-news-Real-Madrid-rule-out-Jese-departure|title=Real Madrid rule out Jese departure|website=Sky Sports|last=Acedo|first=Francisco|date=14 July 2013|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=25 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225145840/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11675/8824111/transfer-news-real-madrid-rule-out-jese-departure|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/1506563/real-madrid-youngster-jese-rodriguez-pens-new-deal|title=Jese pens new deal at Madrid|website=ESPN|last=McMath|first=Duncan|date=24 July 2013|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=23 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160823023715/http://www.espnfc.com/story/1506563/real-madrid-youngster-jese-rodriguez-pens-new-deal|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jesé was handed his [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut on 2 October 2013 by new club manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]], coming on as an 81st-minute substitute for [[Karim Benzema]] in a 4–0 [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|group stage]] victory over [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/380761/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Ronaldo leads Real recovery|website=ESPN|date=2 October 2013|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=28 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128035334/http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/380761/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first competitive goal for Real Madrid in his first [[El Clásico]] appearance on 26 October, netting in [[Overtime (sports)|injury-time]] from a Ronaldo assist in a 2–1 loss at [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/373124/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Alexis chips seals Clasico win|website=ESPN|date=26 October 2013|access-date=26 October 2013|archive-date=23 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131223233906/http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/373124/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 November, Jesé came on as a second-half substitute against [[UD Almería]] and contributed with his first two assists for the first team in a 5–0 away win.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/373084/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Ronaldo injured in Real rout|website=ESPN|date=23 November 2013|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=28 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131128040236/http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/373084/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref> He enjoyed a fine run of form between the back end of 2013 and March 2014, where he netted a late winner at [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], scored his first [[Copa del Rey]] goal in a 2–0 win over [[CA Osasuna]] and netted in league encounters against [[Athletic Bilbao]], [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] and [[Getafe CF|Getafe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/athletic-club-vs-real-madrid/1517859/report|title=Athletic Bilbao 1–1 Real Madrid: Ronaldo sees red as visitors drop points|website=Goal|date=2 February 2014|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=3 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103002923/http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/athletic-club-vs-real-madrid/1517859/report|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26023965|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Villarreal|website=BBC|date=8 February 2014|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=5 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170305201446/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26023965|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/getafe-vs-real-madrid/1517880/report|title=Getafe 0–3 Real Madrid: Blancos breeze past city rivals|website=Goal|date=16 February 2014|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=3 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103003246/http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/getafe-vs-real-madrid/1517880/report|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://msn.foxsports.com/foxsoccer/laliga/story/real-madrid-2-0-osasuna-copa-del-rey-round-of-16-first-leg-karim-benzema-match-report-010914|title=Real defeats Osasuna in Copa del Rey|website=Fox Sports|date=9 January 2014|access-date=10 January 2014|archive-date=10 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110164509/http://msn.foxsports.com/foxsoccer/laliga/story/real-madrid-2-0-osasuna-copa-del-rey-round-of-16-first-leg-karim-benzema-match-report-010914|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 March, however, just two minutes into Real Madrid's Champions League's round-of-16 second leg game against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke]], Jesé suffered a complete tear of the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his right knee following a challenge from [[Sead Kolašinac]] and was sidelined for the remainder of [[2013–14 La Liga|the season]].<ref name=L1314>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/uefa-champions-league/story/1755689/real-madrid-forward-jese-facing-lengthy-injury-lay-off|title=Jese suffers torn ACL; season over|website=ESPN|date=18 March 2014|access-date=19 March 2014|archive-date=27 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227032157/http://www.espnfc.com/uefa-champions-league/story/1755689/real-madrid-forward-jese-facing-lengthy-injury-lay-off|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/03/18/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1395173336.html|title=Jesé, al menos seis meses de baja|trans-title=Jesé, at least six months out|website=Marca|last=Cerezo|first=Hugo|date=18 March 2014|access-date=19 March 2014|language=es|archive-date=27 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170827174035/http://www.marca.com/2014/03/18/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1395173336.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He ended the season with 5 goals and 4 assists to his name in 18 league appearances, and 8 goals in 31 matches across all competitions as Real Madrid went on to lift the Copa Del Rey and Champions League trophies.<ref name=L1314/><ref name=14CL>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27383593|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Atletico Madrid|website=BBC|last=McNulty|first=Phil|date=25 May 2014|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=26 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126180206/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=CDL14>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-za/match/barcelona-vs-real-madrid/1648201/report|title=Barcelona 1–2 Real Madrid: Brilliant Bale breakaway heaps more misery on Martino's men|website=Goal|date=14 April 2014|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=25 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225145344/http://www.goal.com/en-za/match/barcelona-vs-real-madrid/1648201/report|url-status=live}}</ref>

After spending nine months on the sidelines, Jesé returned from injury for the second leg of Real Madrid's tie against [[UE Cornellà]] in the [[Copa del Rey]] round of 32 on 2 December 2014, replacing [[Sami Khedira]] after 57 minutes and scoring the last goal of a 9–1 aggregate victory.<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid 5–0 Cornella (agg 9–1): James shines in Blancos Copa trouncing |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/real-madrid-vs-cornell%C3%A0/1958089/report?ICID=MP_MS_5 |website=Goal |date=2 December 2014 |access-date=24 December 2016 |archive-date=5 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305090226/http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/real-madrid-vs-cornell%C3%A0/1958089/report?ICID=MP_MS_5 |url-status=live }}</ref> On his injury, Jesé stated: "I had a very tough time, but I think that things in life happen for a reason. Maybe I had the injury because I needed to learn and become a more mature footballer."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2014/m=12/news=jese-hitting-the-right-notes-on-and-off-the-pitch-2491784.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215123754/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/y=2014/m=12/news=jese-hitting-the-right-notes-on-and-off-the-pitch-2491784.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 December 2014|title=Jese hitting the right notes on and off the pitch|publisher=FIFA|date=15 December 2014|access-date=16 December 2014}}</ref> Later that month he was included in the club's squad which won the [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup]] in Japan, making a substitute appearance in a 4–0 win over [[Cruz Azul]] in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cruz Azul 0–4 Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30470531 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 December 2014 |access-date=3 August 2015 |archive-date=10 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151010231126/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30470531 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=CWC>{{cite news|url= https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=259701/match=300298898/match-report.html|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20141220234228/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=259701/match=300298898/match-report.html|url-status= dead|archive-date= 20 December 2014|title=Real Madrid coast to Morocco 2014 title|website=FIFA|date=20 December 2014|access-date=25 December 2016}}</ref> He scored the first of his three [[2014–15 La Liga|La Liga]] goals for [[2014–15 Real Madrid C.F. season|the season]] on 4 February 2015 in a 2–1 victory over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-live-blogs/11390564/Real-Madrid-v-Sevilla-La-Liga-Live.html|title=Real Madrid v Sevilla, La Liga: as it happened|date=4 February 2015|website=The Telegraph|last=Eccleshare|first=Charlie|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=26 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160326112916/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/football-live-blogs/11390564/Real-Madrid-v-Sevilla-La-Liga-Live.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé struggled to break back into the first team following his injury though, starting only 3 of his 23 appearances for the season, and by the end of the campaign it was reported that he had grown frustrated at the club and was looking to leave in the summer.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://as.com/diarioas/2015/04/25/english/1429950788_532889.html|title=Jesé fed up at Real Madrid, wants summer exit|date=25 April 2015|website=AS|last=de la Rosa|first=Alvaro|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=30 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730142546/https://as.com/diarioas/2015/04/25/english/1429950788_532889.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://as.com/diarioas/2015/05/16/english/1431759440_918650.html|title=Real Madrid plan to sell Jesé|date=16 May 2015|website=AS|last=de la Rosa|first=Alvaro|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=30 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730154723/https://as.com/diarioas/2015/05/16/english/1431759440_918650.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jesé opted to remain in Madrid for the [[2015–16 La Liga|2015–16 season]] as he sought to break into the first team under new club manager [[Rafael Benítez|Rafa Benítez]]. However, he found competition for places tough and was limited to just 1252 minutes of football across all competitions under Benítez and his successor, [[Zinedine Zidane]]. In spite of his lack of game time, Jesé still managed to contribute 6 goals and 8 assists for the season and was regularly used as a back-up in the team's triumphant [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]] campaign.<ref name=move>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/2923067/jese-rodriguez-seals-move-to--paris-saint-germain-from-real-madrid|title=Jese Rodriguez seals move to Paris Saint-Germain from Real Madrid|website=ESPN|last=Johnson|first=Jonathan|date=8 August 2016|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=25 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225150925/http://www.espnfc.com/story/2923067/jese-rodriguez-seals-move-to--paris-saint-germain-from-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=1516CL>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|date=28 May 2016|website=UEFA|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=14 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814200140/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2016/matches/round=2000638/match=2015789/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

It would ultimately be Jesé's final season at the club as at the end of the season, with one year remaining on his contract, he agreed to sign for reigning [[Ligue 1]] champions [[Paris Saint-Germain]].<ref name=move/> He made 63 La Liga appearances for Real Madrid during his ten-year stay at the [[Santiago Bernabeu Stadium|Santiago Bernabeu]], of which 49 were substitute appearances, and scored 13 goals.<ref name="skysports.com">{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11820/10527956/paris-saint-germain-sign-jese-rodriguez-from-real-madrid|title=Paris Saint-Germain sign Jese Rodriguez from Real Madrid|website=Sky Sports|date=8 August 2016|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=25 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161225145555/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11820/10527956/paris-saint-germain-sign-jese-rodriguez-from-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> In total, across all competitions, Jesé amassed 96 appearances and 18 goals for the club, departing with two Champions League titles and one apiece in La Liga, the Copa Del Rey and the Club World Cup to his name.<ref name=SW>{{cite web|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/jesse-rodriguez-ruiz/160640/|title=Jesé Rodríguez|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=15 May 2013|archive-date=10 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710173837/http://uk.soccerway.com/players/jesse-rodriguez-ruiz/160640/|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:2019-07-17 SG Dynamo Dresden vs. Paris Saint-Germain by Sandro Halank–417.jpg|thumb|289x289px|Jesé playing for [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2019]]

===Paris Saint-Germain===
On 8 August 2016, Jesé joined French side [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on a five-year deal for a reported transfer fee of €25 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/08/official-announcement-jese-rodriguez|title=Official Announcement: Jesé Rodríguez|date=8 August 2016|website=Real Madrid Football Club|access-date=8 August 2016|archive-date=11 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811202634/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/08/official-announcement-jese-rodriguez|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/76470/Jese-signs-5-year-contract-with-Paris-Saint-Germain|title=Jesé signs 5-year contract with Paris Saint-Germain|work=Paris Saint-Germain - PSG |date=8 August 2016|publisher=psg.fr|access-date=8 August 2016|archive-date=8 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808171801/http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/76470/Jese-signs-5-year-contract-with-Paris-Saint-Germain|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="skysports.com"/> The deal included an 'anti-Barcelona' clause which prevented PSG from selling Jesé to Real Madrid's fierce La Liga rivals Barcelona in the future.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.squawka.com/news/jese-contract-to-contain-anti-barca-clause/739167|title=Jese Rodriguez's Paris Saint-Germain contract to contain anti-Barcelona clause – report|website=Squawka|last=Moalim|first=Mohamed|date=4 August 2016|access-date=27 December 2016|archive-date=27 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227201027/http://www.squawka.com/news/jese-contract-to-contain-anti-barca-clause/739167|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut on 13 August, coming on as a substitute for [[Hatem Ben Arfa]] in a 1–0 away win over [[SC Bastia|Bastia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/bastia-vs-psg/50460|title=French Ligue 1 (Sky Sports)|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-date=3 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200303084408/https://www.skysports.com/football/bastia-vs-psg/50460|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé was ruled out for a short period soon thereafter as a result of him suffering from [[appendicitis]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1722/ligue-1/2016/09/12/27418762/jese-not-at-psg-to-play-second-string-to-cavani|title=Jese not at PSG to play second string to Cavani|website=Goal|last=Farrel|first=Dom|date=12 September 2016|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=24 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224233130/http://www.goal.com/en/news/1722/ligue-1/2016/09/12/27418762/jese-not-at-psg-to-play-second-string-to-cavani|url-status=live}}</ref> Following his return, he scored his first goal for the club on 19 November, netting from the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty-spot]] in a 2–0 win over [[FC Nantes|Nantes]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/french-ligue-1/story/3000050/angel-di-maria-jese-rodriguez-on-target-to-help-psg-defeat-nantes|title=Angel Di Maria, Jese Rodriguez on target to help PSG defeat Nantes|website=ESPN|date=19 November 2016|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=24 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224165147/http://www.espnfc.com/french-ligue-1/story/3000050/angel-di-maria-jese-rodriguez-on-target-to-help-psg-defeat-nantes|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his [[Coupe de la Ligue]] debut on 14 December and scored the third goal in a 3–1 win over [[LOSC Lille|Lille]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.beinsports.com/us/french-cup/video/jese-scores-as-psg-defeat-lille-advance-in-co/394553|title=Jese Scores as PSG Defeat Lille; Advance in Coupe De La Ligue|website=beIN|date=14 December 2016|access-date=24 December 2016|archive-date=24 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224233753/http://www.beinsports.com/us/french-cup/video/jese-scores-as-psg-defeat-lille-advance-in-co/394553|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jesé struggled to settle in Paris, however, and by the end of the year he had only started in one of his nine league appearances for the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.squawka.com/news/psg-chairman-suggests-club-made-a-mistake-signing-jese-from-real-madrid/861434|title=PSG chairman suggests club "made a mistake" signing Jese from Real Madrid|website=Squawka|last=Hamouda|first=Omar|date=24 December 2016|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=3 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103094716/http://www.squawka.com/news/psg-chairman-suggests-club-made-a-mistake-signing-jese-from-real-madrid/861434|url-status=live}}</ref> His lack of form and infrequent game time, which totaled 358 minutes, prompted manager [[Unai Emery]] to suggest that he would be leaving the club during the January [[transfer window]] in order to rediscover his form.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/3033241/jese-rodriguez-could-leave-paris-saint-germain-this-month-unai-emery|title=Jese Rodriguez could leave Paris Saint-Germain this month – Unai Emery|website=ESPN|last=Johnson|first=Jonathan|date=6 January 2017|access-date=31 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202122943/http://www.espnfc.com/story/3033241/jese-rodriguez-could-leave-paris-saint-germain-this-month-unai-emery|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2017/07/17/596c8d2122601d3f738b4631.html|title=Ten top players searching for a new team|website=Marca|last=Prada|first=Jon|date=17 July 2017|access-date=19 July 2017|archive-date=19 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170719005951/http://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2017/07/17/596c8d2122601d3f738b4631.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2017: Loan to Las Palmas====
On 31 January 2017, Jesé signed for [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] on loan until the end of the season. Club chairman Miguel Ángel Ramírez revealed that he had taken a massive pay cut in order to join his hometown club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/story/3050102/paris-saint-germain-forward-jese-joins-las-palmas-on-loan|title=Paris Saint-Germain forward Jese joins Las Palmas on loan|website=ESPN|last=Garcia|first=Adriana|date=31 January 2017|access-date=31 January 2017|archive-date=1 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170201150539/http://www.espnfc.us/story/3050102/paris-saint-germain-forward-jese-joins-las-palmas-on-loan|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/soccer-transfers/story/3049664/jese-rodriguez-to-take-pay-cut-to-join-las-palmas-on-loan-from-psg|title=Jese Rodriguez to take pay cut to join Las Palmas on loan from PSG|website=ESPN|last=Garcia|first=Adriana|date=30 January 2017|access-date=31 January 2017|archive-date=1 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170201114952/http://www.espnfc.us/soccer-transfers/story/3049664/jese-rodriguez-to-take-pay-cut-to-join-las-palmas-on-loan-from-psg|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, he was presented in front of 9,000 fans at the [[Estadio de Gran Canaria]], and pledged to do all he could to help the club qualify for [[UEFA Europa League|European football]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Garcia|first1=Adriana|title=Jese Rodriguez not eager for Paris Saint-Germain return|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/3051357/jese-rodriguez-not-eager-for-paris-saint-germain-return-after-las-palmas-loan|website=ESPN|date=1 February 2017|access-date=1 February 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202100334/http://www.espnfc.com/story/3051357/jese-rodriguez-not-eager-for-paris-saint-germain-return-after-las-palmas-loan|url-status=live}}</ref> He debuted for the club on 6 February, coming on as a second-half substitute for [[Vicente Gómez Umpiérrez|Vicente Gómez]] in a 1–0 loss away to [[Granada CF|Granada]], and made his first start the following week in a loss to [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] by the same scoreline.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2017/02/06/5898ed6d468aeb5f1f8b45a7.html|title=Jese Rodriguez misses absolute sitter as Las Palmas lose at lowly Granada|website=Marca|last=Mayo|first=Marc|date=6 February 2017|access-date=7 February 2017|archive-date=7 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207113346/http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2017/02/06/5898ed6d468aeb5f1f8b45a7.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.firstpost.com/sports/la-liga-roundup-atletico-madrid-reclaim-fourth-spot-sevilla-snatch-late-winner-against-las-palmas-3280022.html|title=La Liga roundup: Atletico Madrid reclaim fourth spot, Sevilla snatch late winner against Las Palmas|website=First Post|date=13 February 2017|access-date=17 February 2017|archive-date=18 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170218063712/http://www.firstpost.com/sports/la-liga-roundup-atletico-madrid-reclaim-fourth-spot-sevilla-snatch-late-winner-against-las-palmas-3280022.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 1 March, Jesé returned to the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] for the first time ahead of Las Palmas' La Liga encounter with Real Madrid. During the build-up to the match, he revealed that he owed a debt to Real Madrid for welcoming him at the club and blamed the cruciate ligament injury he suffered as the reason for him not becoming a star with them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/las-palmas/story/3071478/jese-rodriguez-blames-injury-for-curtailing-real-madrid-career|title=Jese Rodriguez blames injury for curtailing Real Madrid career|website=ESPN|date=1 March 2017|access-date=2 March 2017|archive-date=2 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302095948/http://www.espnfc.com/las-palmas/story/3071478/jese-rodriguez-blames-injury-for-curtailing-real-madrid-career|url-status=live}}</ref> He also defended his previous criticism of former manager José Mourinho, stating that he has no regrets over his actions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/722/la-liga/2017/03/01/33188002/jese-does-not-regret-mourinho-criticism|title=Jese does not regret Mourinho criticism|website=Goal|last=Coerts|first=Stefan|date=1 March 2017|access-date=2 March 2017|archive-date=2 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302194428/http://www.goal.com/en/news/722/la-liga/2017/03/01/33188002/jese-does-not-regret-mourinho-criticism|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé started in the match between the two sides which ultimately ended in a 3–3 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/real-madrid-vs-las-palmas/2283148/report|title=Real Madrid 3–3 Las Palmas: Late show Ronaldo rescues point for 10-man Madrid|website=Goal|date=1 March 2017|access-date=2 March 2017|archive-date=3 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303044137/http://www.goal.com/en/match/real-madrid-vs-las-palmas/2283148/report|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first goals for the club four days later, netting a brace in a 5–2 league win over [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]]. The result was Jesé's first win with Las Palmas, after the club failed to record a victory in its previous five matches following his arrival.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Las-palmas-bat-osasuna-5-2-jese-marque-un-double/783248|title=Las Palmas bat Osasuna 5–2, Jesé marque un doublé|website=L'Equipe|date=5 March 2017|language=fr|access-date=5 March 2017|archive-date=6 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170306033907/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Las-palmas-bat-osasuna-5-2-jese-marque-un-double/783248|url-status=live}}</ref> He ultimately made 16 appearances for the campaign, scoring three goals and registering an [[Assist (football)|assist]] as the side dropped to end the season in fourteenth position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-espana.net/64198/la-liga-week-38-saturday-review|title=La Liga Week 38 Saturday Review|website=Football Espana|date=21 May 2017|access-date=23 May 2017|archive-date=9 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170609065702/http://www.football-espana.net/64198/la-liga-week-38-saturday-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Upon the conclusion of Jesé's loan agreement, Las Palmas elected not to attempt to sign him permanently, with his poor overall performance, high salary demands and off-field behaviour ultimately contributing to the club's decision.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canarias7.es/deportes/futbol/no-a-jese-y-araujo-vuelve-bajo-advertencia-JA1288496|title=No a Jesé y Araujo vuelve bajo advertencia|website=Canarias 7|date=22 June 2017|language=es|access-date=29 June 2017|archive-date=22 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170622104715/https://www.canarias7.es/deportes/futbol/no-a-jese-y-araujo-vuelve-bajo-advertencia-JA1288496|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2017–18: Loan to Stoke City====
On 16 August 2017, Jesé joined [[Premier League]] club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on loan for the [[2017–18 Stoke City F.C. season|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/40922444|title=Jese Rodriguez: Stoke sign PSG forward on loan|website=BBC Sport|date=16 August 2017|access-date=16 August 2017|archive-date=16 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816162057/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/40922444|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite having only trained once with the team following his arrival, he made his debut on 19 August and scored the only goal in a 1–0 win over [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Stoke 1–0 Arsenal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40908333|website=BBC Sport|last=Jurjko|first=Jonathan|date=19 August 2017|access-date=19 August 2017|archive-date=19 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819183611/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40908333|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/stoke-vs-arsenal-five-things-we-learned-score-result-jese-danny-welbeck-alexandre-lacazette-goal-a7902721.html|title=Stoke vs Arsenal: Five things we learned as Jese Rodriguez makes debut to remember as wasteful Gunners lose|website=Independent|last=de Menezes|first=Jack|date=19 August 2017|access-date=19 August 2017|archive-date=19 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170819232806/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/stoke-vs-arsenal-five-things-we-learned-score-result-jese-danny-welbeck-alexandre-lacazette-goal-a7902721.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://kwese.espn.com/football/blog/the-match/60/post/3182937/arsenal-stumble-at-stoke-as-jese-makes-dream-potters-debut|title=Arsenal stumble at Stoke as Jese makes dream Potters debut|website=ESPN|last=Brewin|first=John|date=19 August 2017|access-date=20 August 2017|archive-date=20 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820120222/http://kwese.espn.com/football/blog/the-match/60/post/3182937/arsenal-stumble-at-stoke-as-jese-makes-dream-potters-debut|url-status=live}}</ref> In December 2017, Jesé left the stadium early during Stoke's match against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] after manager [[Mark Hughes]] made all of his substitutes and left him on the bench. He was subsequently disciplined by the club. In unrelated circumstances, he missed the next match against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and a number of subsequent matches as he had been granted compassionate leave to visit his prematurely born son in the Canary Islands.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42272882|title=Jese Rodriguez: Stoke discipline striker after walk-out|website=BBC Sport|date=7 December 2017|access-date=10 December 2017|archive-date=11 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211102203/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42272882|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=CL>{{cite web|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stoke-transfer-news-jese-psg-1095798|title=Jese Rodriguez returns to training at Stoke City – with message of thanks to fans and club|website=Stoke Sentinel|last=Smith|first=Peter|date=21 January 2018|access-date=25 January 2018|archive-date=24 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180124081744/http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stoke-transfer-news-jese-psg-1095798|url-status=live}}</ref>

He made his return on 10 February 2018 in Stoke's 1–1 draw with [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]] and in the final minutes of the match won a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] after being fouled by [[Dale Stephens (footballer)|Dale Stephens]]. Teammate, and regular Stoke penalty-taker, [[Charlie Adam]] denied a visibly angered Jesé the opportunity the take the penalty but saw his effort saved by Brighton [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Mathew Ryan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/11245367/jese-rodriguez-in-stoke-city-penalty-bust-up-against-brighton|title=Jese Rodriguez in Stoke City penalty bust-up against Brighton|website=Sky Sports|date=11 February 2018|access-date=11 February 2018|archive-date=12 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180212005036/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/11245367/jese-rodriguez-in-stoke-city-penalty-bust-up-against-brighton|url-status=live}}</ref> New club manager [[Paul Lambert]] later denied that there was any rift between the players following the match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/02/11/paul-lambert-insists-penalty-row-charlie-adam-jese-rodriguez/|title=Paul Lambert insists penalty row between Charlie Adam and Jese Rodriguez will not affect Stoke|work=The Telegraph|last=Percy|first=John|date=11 February 2018|access-date=17 April 2018|archive-date=18 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418020703/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/02/11/paul-lambert-insists-penalty-row-charlie-adam-jese-rodriguez/|url-status=live}}</ref> The following month, Jesé was again afforded compassionate leave after his son underwent a second operation. However, he failed to return to training thereafter which sparked speculation that Stoke would look to terminate his loan contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/04/12/paul-lambert-insists-stoke-have-no-disciplinary-problem-despitejese/|title=Paul Lambert insists Stoke have no disciplinary problem despite Jese Rodriguez's continued no-show|work=The Telegraph|last=Percy|first=John|date=12 April 2018|access-date=17 April 2018|archive-date=18 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180418064759/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/04/12/paul-lambert-insists-stoke-have-no-disciplinary-problem-despitejese/|url-status=live}}</ref> His loan spell ended on 1 May when the club confirmed that he had been given unpaid compassionate leave until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43967077|title=Jese Rodriguez leaves Stoke after being granted compassionate leave|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 May 2018|access-date=2 May 2018|archive-date=2 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502043027/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43967077|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/11355041/jese-rodriguez-given-compassionate-leave-as-stoke-loan-spell-ends|title=Stoke grant Jese Rodriguez compassionate leave as loan ends|publisher=Sky Sports|date=2 May 2018|access-date=2 May 2018|archive-date=1 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501191620/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/11355041/jese-rodriguez-given-compassionate-leave-as-stoke-loan-spell-ends|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored one goal in 13 appearances during his time with Stoke and the club ultimately suffered relegation from the Premier League.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-za/news/psg-forward-jese-sees-difficult-stoke-loan-spell-terminated/tvb0j8qun6831s1h3ux4t6hi7|title=PSG forward Jese sees difficult Stoke loan spell terminated|publisher=Goal|last=Burton|first=Chris|date=1 May 2018|access-date=2 May 2018|archive-date=2 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502211232/http://www.goal.com/en-za/news/psg-forward-jese-sees-difficult-stoke-loan-spell-terminated/tvb0j8qun6831s1h3ux4t6hi7|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44017611|title=Stoke relegated from Premier League: Paul Lambert says club 'too big' to stay down|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 May 2018|access-date=7 May 2018|archive-date=11 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180511153221/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44017611|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2018–19: Return to PSG and loan to Betis====

Upon his return to PSG, Jesé indicated his eagerness to fight for a spot in the team but he and teammate [[Gonçalo Guedes]] were later excluded from new manager [[Thomas Tuchel]]'s pre-season tour of Asia.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2018/07/24/5b574ec6e5fdeaa9738b4615.html|title=Guedes and Jese set to depart PSG as Tuchel excludes duo from pre-season tour|work=Marca|last=Kostopoulos|first=Panos|date=24 July 2018|access-date=27 July 2018|archive-date=26 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726182704/http://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2018/07/24/5b574ec6e5fdeaa9738b4615.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He continued to be excluded as the season commenced and was also made to train alone by Tuchel alongside [[Jean-Christophe Bahebeck]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://kwese.espn.com/football/paris-saint-germain/story/3593840/psgs-kylian-mbappe-and-france-world-cup-winners-skip-ligue-1-opener-vs-caen|title=PSG's Kylian Mbappe, France World Cup winners skip Ligue 1 opener vs. Caen|publisher=ESPN|last=Johnson|first=Jonathan|date=12 August 2018|access-date=13 August 2018|archive-date=12 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812193706/http://kwese.espn.com/football/paris-saint-germain/story/3593840/psgs-kylian-mbappe-and-france-world-cup-winners-skip-ligue-1-opener-vs-caen|url-status=live}}</ref> At the turn of the year, with Jesé having not played a single match for the season, it was revealed that he had lost 7&nbsp;kg after appointing a personal trainer as he looked to reintegrate himself into the team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.football-espana.net/76209/jese-rodriguez-given-paris-saint-germain-lifeline|title=Jese Rodriguez given Paris Saint-Germain lifeline?|publisher=Football Espana|date=6 January 2019|access-date=8 January 2019|archive-date=8 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190108200718/https://www.football-espana.net/76209/jese-rodriguez-given-paris-saint-germain-lifeline|url-status=live}}</ref> He then made his first, and only appearance for the club for the season on 23 January 2019, coming on as a last minute substitute in a [[Coupe de France]] win over [[Racing Club de Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47050961|title=Jese Rodriguez: Paris St-Germain forward joins Real Betis on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 January 2019|access-date=30 January 2019|archive-date=30 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190130180452/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47050961|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 29 January, Jesé signed for [[Real Betis|Betis]] on loan until the end of the season where he reunited with former Las Palmas manager, [[Quique Setién]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en-za/news/psg-reject-jese-seals-loan-transfer-to-betis/12rnl2zvxjlg71cl3wpb86787x|title=PSG reject Jese seals loan transfer to Betis|publisher=Goal|date=29 January 2019|access-date=30 January 2019|archive-date=30 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190130162344/https://www.goal.com/en-za/news/psg-reject-jese-seals-loan-transfer-to-betis/12rnl2zvxjlg71cl3wpb86787x|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/01/29/5c50b227268e3efe528b461f.html|title=Official: Jese joins Real Betis on loan|work=Marca|last=Cerezeo|first=Hugo|date=29 January 2019|access-date=31 January 2019|archive-date=31 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190131010718/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/01/29/5c50b227268e3efe528b461f.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 7 February, coming on as a second-half substitute in a 2–2 Copa del Rey draw with [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/20190207/debut-jese-rodriguez-betis/374463877_0.html|title=Así fue el debut de Jesé Rodríguez con el Betis|work=El Espanol|last=Santiago|first=Ruben|date=7 February 2019|access-date=8 February 2019|language=es|archive-date=9 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190209124039/https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/20190207/debut-jese-rodriguez-betis/374463877_0.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The following week, he made his [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] debut as a second-half substitute and assisted [[Diego Lainez]] for an injury-time equalizer in a 3–3 draw with [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=530668|title=Diego Lainez's late goal salvages draw for Real Betis vs. Stade Rennes|publisher=ESPN|date=14 February 2019|access-date=15 February 2019|archive-date=14 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190214234154/http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=530668|url-status=live}}</ref> His first goal followed on 10 March, when he scored the only goal in a 1–0 league win over [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailymercato.com/news/jese-rodriguez-a-marque-son-premier-but-avec-le-betis-seville|title=Jesé Rodriguez a marqué son premier but avec le Betis Séville|last=Borne|first=Fabien|date=10 March 2019 |language=en |work=Daily Mercato |access-date=10 March 2019}}</ref> He ultimately scored twice in eighteen appearances but Betis elected not to sign him permanently at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mercato365.com/leeds-pense-a-jese-9125149.html|title=Leeds pensa a Jese|publisher=Mercato 365|date=26 May 2019|language=es|access-date=7 June 2019|archive-date=25 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190525232423/https://www.mercato365.com/leeds-pense-a-jese-9125149.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2019–20: Loan to Sporting CP====
On 2 September 2019, Jesé joined Portuguese club [[Sporting CP]] on loan for the [[2019–20 Sporting CP season|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sporting.pt/pt/noticias/futebol/equipa-principal/2019-09-02/jese-o-sporting-cp-e-um-clube-historico |title=Jesé: "O Sporting CP é um Clube histórico" |trans-title=Jesé: "Sporting CP is a historic club" |language=pt |publisher=[[Sporting CP]] |date=2 September 2019 |access-date=2 September 2019 |archive-date=2 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902215846/https://www.sporting.pt/pt/noticias/futebol/equipa-principal/2019-09-02/jese-o-sporting-cp-e-um-clube-historico |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club towards the end of the following month, opening the scoring in a 3–1 win over [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://videos.marca.com/v/0_qsgovnrv-golazo-de-jese-en-portugal-ojo-como-sento-al-portero?count=0|title=Golazo de Jesé en Portugal! Ojo cómo sentó al portero...|trans-title=Jesé great goal in Portugal! Watch how he sat the goalkeeper|work=Marca|language=es|date=27 October 2019|access-date=28 October 2019|archive-date=29 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200229091329/https://videos.marca.com/v/0_qsgovnrv-golazo-de-jese-en-portugal-ojo-como-sento-al-portero?count=0|url-status=live}}</ref>

At the end of the [[2019–20 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season|2019–20]] season, Jesé received a [[Ligue 1]] medal for his contributions at PSG, where he played one minute the whole season in an away match against [[FC Metz|Metz]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=PSG: Jese Rodriguez will receive 19/20 Ligue 1 winners' medal after playing just one minute|url=https://www.givemesport.com/1566470-psg-jese-rodriguez-will-receive-1920-ligue-1-winners-medal-after-playing-just-one-minute|website=GiveMeSport|date=2 May 2020|access-date=4 May 2020|archive-date=4 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200504043925/https://www.givemesport.com/1566470-psg-jese-rodriguez-will-receive-1920-ligue-1-winners-medal-after-playing-just-one-minute|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== 2020–21: Contract termination ====
Jesé did not complete a permanent transfer to Sporting CP after the end of his loan deal; instead, he headed back to PSG. On 10 September 2020, Jesé made his return to play for the Parisian club in a 1–0 loss to [[RC Lens|Lens]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Zavala|first=Steve|date=10 September 2020|title=Jese Rodriguez Made his Return to Action with PSG During the Club's 1–0 Loss to Lens|url=https://psgtalk.com/2020/09/jese-rodriguez-made-his-return-to-action-with-psg-during-the-clubs-1-0-loss-to-lens/|access-date=30 September 2020|website=PSG Talk}}</ref> He made his final appearance for PSG as a substitute in a 4–0 win against [[Nîmes Olympique|Nîmes]] on 16 October.<ref>{{Cite web|date=16 October 2020|title=Nimes vs. Paris Saint-Germain|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/lineups?gameId=573211|website=ESPN}}</ref>

On 6 December, Paris Saint-Germain announced the termination of his contract by mutual agreement.<ref name="psgconter">{{cite web|date=6 December 2020|title=Jesé Rodriguez quitte le Paris Saint-Germain|trans-title=Jesé Rodríguez quits Paris Saint-Germain|url=https://www.psg.fr/equipes/equipe-premiere/content/jese-rodriguez-quitte-le-paris-saint-germain-officiel-psg|access-date=6 December 2020|website=Paris Saint-Germain|language=Fr|archive-date=28 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128132236/https://www.psg.fr/equipes/equipe-premiere/content/jese-rodriguez-quitte-le-paris-saint-germain-officiel-psg|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Second stint at Las Palmas===
On 1 February 2021, Jesé returned to [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|date=1 February 2021|title=Jesé, nuevo jugador de la UD Las Palmas|trans-title=Jesé, new player of UD Las Palmas|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/noticias/noticia/jese-nuevo-jugador-de-la-ud-las-palmas|access-date=1 February 2021|website=UD Las Palmas|language=es|archive-date=1 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201204642/https://www.udlaspalmas.es/noticias/noticia/jese-nuevo-jugador-de-la-ud-las-palmas|url-status=live}}</ref> He put up a 'man of the match' performance where he scored a goal and also assisted in the 6–1 victory over [[CD Lugo|Lugo]] on 1 April.

=== Ankaragücü ===
Jesé joined Turkish [[Süper Lig]] club [[MKE Ankaragücü|Ankaragücü]] on 4 August 2022, signing a one-year deal with the club.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Tiryaki |first1=Erkan |title=Jese Rodriguez will do everything he can for Ankaragucu fans |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/jese-rodriguez-will-do-everything-he-can-for-ankaragucu-fans/2653393# |access-date=9 September 2022 |work=Anadolu Agency |date=4 August 2022}}</ref> He made his competitive debut four days later, coming on as a substitute for [[Giorgi Beridze]] in the 61st minute of a 0–0 home draw against [[Konyaspor]].<ref>{{cite news |title=(ÖZET) Ankaragücü – Konyaspor maç sonucu: 0–0 |url=https://www.fanatik.com.tr/ozet-ankaragucu-konyaspor-mac-sonucu-0-0-2295444 |access-date=9 September 2022 |work=Fanatik |date=8 August 2022 |language=tr}}</ref> On 8 November, Jesé scored a brace during the [[2022–23 Turkish Cup]] in a 6–2 win over [[Amed Sportif]]. However, his contract was terminated early by mutual consent on 13 January 2023.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Ankaragücü|url=https://www.facebook.com/Ankaragucu/posts/pfbid0GYqV14daWRhARHhzgh7uhgRaiGNH8kHNg2RWKkYtJxRrg1wvA6aQinR1eS64Stmxl|title=Kulübümüz ile Jesé Rodríguez arasındaki sözleşmenin, karşılıklı anlaşılarak sona erdirilmesi konusunda mutabakata varılmıştır.|date=13 January 2023|access-date=23 January 2023|language=tr}}</ref>

=== Sampdoria ===
On 10 February 2023, Jesé joined [[Serie A]] club [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] on a contract until the end of the season, with the option of a further year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sampdoria, confirmada la contratación de Jesé|url=https://www.todomercadoweb.es/primer-plano/oficial-sampdoria-confirmada-la-contratacion-de-jese-443414 |access-date=10 February 2023 |work=todomercadoweb |date=10 February 2023 |language=es}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the Italian side on 16 April, in a 1–1 [[2022–23 Serie A|league]] draw against [[US Lecce|Lecce]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spigno |first=Gregorio |date=16 April 2023 |title=Lecce Sampdoria 1-1, gol di Ceesay e Jesé Rodriguez |url=https://www.corriere.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/23_aprile_16/lecce-sampdoria-risultato-1-1-gol-ceesay-jese-rodriguez-5d93aff4-dc4e-11ed-a957-6a12e2c879aa.shtml |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=Corriere della Sera |language=it-IT}}</ref>

=== Coritiba ===
On 6 September 2023, Jesé joined [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] club [[Coritiba Foot Ball Club|Coritiba]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]], signing a contract until the end of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sànchez |first=Virtudes |date=6 September 2023 |title=Jesé Rodríguez ficha por el Coritiba de Brasil |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/futbol-internacional/2023/09/06/64f892c0e2704e2db18b45bc.html |access-date=8 September 2023 |website=MARCA |language=es-ES}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 2–1 lost against [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] on 26 November.

=== Johor Darul Ta'zim ===
After 10 months without a club, Jesé joined [[Malaysia Super League]] club [[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]] on 5 October 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bernama.com/en/news.php?id=2348282|title=JDT Snap Up Ex-Real Madrid Ace Jese Rodriguez|language=en|website=bernama.com|date=5 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Former Real Madrid & PSG star Jese completes bizarre transfer as nomadic career takes fresh twist|date=5 October 2024|publisher=Goal.com|url=https://www.goal.com/en-my/lists/former-real-madrid-psg-star-jese-bizarre-transfer-nomadic-career-fresh-twist/bltd80000bd92ec68cb}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Former Real Madrid striker Jesé Rodríguez signs for Malaysian club Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|date=5 October 2024|publisher=Fabrizio Romano|url=https://x.com/FabrizioRomano/status/1842530390772166971}}</ref> He make his club debut on 22 October in the [[2024–25 AFC Champions League Elite]] against Korean club [[Gwangju FC|Gwangju]]. Jesé then made his [[2024–25 Malaysia Super League|league]] debut on 1 November in a 4–0 away win against [[Negeri Sembilan FC|Negeri Sembilan]]. On 30 November, he scored his first goal for the club during the [[2024–25 Malaysia Cup]] round of 16 tie against [[Kuala Lumpur Rovers F.C.|Kuala Lumpur Rovers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=1 December 2024 |title=Rodriguez savours first goal with JDT in rout of Rovers |url=https://www.thestar.com.my/sport/football/2024/12/01/rodriguez-savours-first-goal-with-jdt-in-rout-of-rovers |website=thestar.com.my |language=en}}</ref> On 5 February 2025, he scored his first league goal by scoring the third goal in a 4–0 home win against [[Polis Diraja Malaysia FC|PDRM]]. On 18 February, Jesé then scored his first AFC Champions League Elite goal in the stoppage time against Korean club [[Pohang Steelers]] which his club went on to win 5–2 thus qualifying to the round of 16. He then won the league title and the league cup in his first season with JDT.

===Third stint at Las Palmas===
On 24 July 2025, Jesé returned to Las Palmas on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/noticias/jese-rodriguez-y-la-ud-las-palmas-unen-sus-caminos|title=Jesé Rodríguez y la UD Las Palmas unen sus caminos|trans-title=Jesé Rodríguez and UD Las Palmas join their paths|publisher=UD Las Palmas|language=es|date=24 July 2025|accessdate=25 July 2025}}</ref> On 25 June of the following year, after being regularly used, he renewed his link until 2028.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/noticias/jese-rodriguez-renueva-su-vinculacion-con-la-ud-las-palmas-hasta-2028|title=Jesé Rodríguez renueva su vinculación con la UD Las Palmas hasta 2028|trans-title=Jesé Rodríguez renews his link with UD Las Palmas until 2028|publisher=UD Las Palmas|language=es|date=25 June 2026|accessdate=27 June 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
===Spain national youth teams===
[[File:Jesé Rodríguez and Gerard Deloufeu.jpg|thumb|upright|Jesé with [[Gerard Deulofeu]] at the [[2012 UEFA European Under-19 Football Championship|European Under-19 Championship]] in 2012.]]
Jesé is a former [[Spain national youth football team (disambiguation)|Spanish youth international]], having represented the nation at all levels from the [[Spain national under-16 football team|under-16s]] to the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21s]] between 2009 and 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=250016661/profile/index.html|title=Jesé|website=UEFA|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=8 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108042905/http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=250016661/profile/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2010, he traveled to Liechtenstein with the [[Spain national under-17 football team|Spain under-17 side]] for the [[2010 UEFA European Under-17 Football Championship|2010 UEFA European Football Championship]] in which Spain ended as runners-up to [[England national under-17 football team|England]]. Jesé scored one goal at the tournament, netting the opener in Spain's 3–1 semi-final win over [[Turkey national under-17 football team|Turkey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330004812309/noticia/Noticia/Jese_Rodriguez_y_Alfonso_Herrero,_convocados_con_la_Sub-17_de_Espana.htm|title=Jesé Rodríguez y Alfonso Herrero, convocados con la Sub-17 de España|trans-title=Jesé Rodríguez and Alfonso Herrero, calledup by Spain under-17|website=Real Madrid|date=9 May 2010|access-date=4 June 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004231448/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1330004812309/noticia/Noticia/Jese_Rodriguez_y_Alfonso_Herrero,_convocados_con_la_Sub-17_de_Espana.htm|archive-date=4 October 2013|language=es}}</ref><ref name="PROVINCIA">{{cite web|url=http://www.laprovincia.es/deportes/2010/06/22/gran-sueno-debutar-bernabeu/308674.html|title=´Mi gran sueño, debutar en el Bernabéu´|trans-title=´My biggest dream, play my first game at the Bernabéu´|website=La Provincia|date=22 June 2010|language=es|access-date=4 June 2013|archive-date=29 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029211323/http://www.laprovincia.es/deportes/2010/06/22/gran-sueno-debutar-bernabeu/308674.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://spanishfootballsports.blogspot.co.za/2010/05/spanish-national-football-team-euro-u17.html|title=Spanish National Football Team – Euro U/17 Semi Final – Spain 3 Turkey 1 – Into the Final|website=Spanish Football Sports|date=28 May 2010|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=26 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226055323/http://spanishfootballsports.blogspot.co.za/2010/05/spanish-national-football-team-euro-u17.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Two years later, Jesé netted five goals during Spain's victorious [[2012 UEFA European Under-19 Football Championship|2012 European Under-19 Championship]] campaign in [[Estonia]], including a [[hat trick]] against [[Portugal national under-19 football team|Portugal]] and the winning goal against [[Greece national under-19 football team|Greece]] in the final. Jesé also received the Golden Boot award for ending as the competition's top goalscorer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/match/2010336--portugal-vs-spain/|title=João Mário steals Spain's thunder|website=UEFA|date=6 July 2012|access-date=9 July 2012|archive-date=2 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802111128/http://www.uefa.com/under19/season=2012/matches/round=2000210/match=2010336/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="JOY">{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/news/0257-0deb6561d20d-5227e12bb58c-1000--more-joy-for-spain-s-jese-with-u19-scoring-honour/|title=More joy for Spain's Jesé with U19 scoring honour|website=UEFA|date=15 July 2012|access-date=25 December 2016|archive-date=25 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425181436/https://www.uefa.com/under19/news/newsid=1840961.html#jese+takes+scoring+honour|url-status=live}}</ref> The following year, Jesé scored a further five goals and assisted another for the [[Spain national under-20 football team|Spain under-20 team]] at the [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in [[Turkey]]. Spain were ultimately eliminated at hands of [[Uruguay national under-20 football team|Uruguay]] in the quarter-finals but the nation's early exit from the competition did not prevent Jesé from earning the Bronze Boot award for ending as the tournament's third top goalscorer.<ref name="U20">{{cite web|url=http://as.com/diarioas/2013/07/05/english/1373050659_943906.html|title=Jesé scaling heights of Maradona and Messi at under-20 World Cup|website=Diario AS|last=Gabilondo|first=Aritz|date=5 July 2013|access-date=10 July 2013|archive-date=10 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130710194317/http://as.com/diarioas/2013/07/05/english/1373050659_943906.html|url-status=live}}</ref> His form at the tournament drew praise from Spanish journalist [[Guillem Balagué]] who claimed he was better than Real Madrid's new [[World football transfer record|world-record]] signing [[Gareth Bale]] was at the same age.<ref name="U20FIFA">{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/18232/9182848/better-than-bale|title=Better than Bale?|website=SkySports|last1=Balague|first1=Guillem|last2=Bate|first2=Adam|date=25 February 2014|access-date=22 August 2014|archive-date=15 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150115102758/http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/18232/9182848/better-than-bale|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 February 2014, although he was still eligible to play for [[Spain national under-21 football team|the under-21s]], [[Spain national football team|Spain]] manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] revealed that Jesé was in his plans ahead of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] in [[Brazil]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/97137/del-bosque-signals-jese-is-an-option-for-spain/|title=Del Bosque signals Jesé is an option for Spain|publisher=Inside Spanish Football|date=6 February 2014|access-date=9 February 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140206154301/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/97137/del-bosque-signals-jese-is-an-option-for-spain/|archive-date=6 February 2014}}</ref> However, his chances of taking part at the tournament were ended in March when he ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament while playing for Real Madrid, with Del Bosque describing the situation as "a blow".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/101347/del-bosque-admits-jese-knee-injury-is-a-blow/|title=Del Bosque admits Jesé knee injury is a "blow"|publisher=Inside Spanish Football|date=19 March 2014|access-date=20 March 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140320035910/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/101347/del-bosque-admits-jese-knee-injury-is-a-blow/|archive-date=20 March 2014}}</ref> Due to his eight-month spell on the sidelines, Jesé also missed Spain's [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification play-offs|qualification play-off]] against [[Serbia national under-21 football team|Serbia]] for the [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2015 European U-21 Championship]]. Spain ultimately lost the match 2–1 and thereby also failed to qualify for the [[Football at the 2016 Summer Olympics|2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2014/12/02/en/football/real_madrid/1417514236.html|title=A new and improved Jesé|publisher=Marca (English)|date=2 December 2014|access-date=2 December 2014|archive-date=2 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141202170204/http://www.marca.com/en/2014/12/02/en/football/real_madrid/1417514236.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[File:Jesé Rodríguez and Tiago Ilori.jpg|thumb|right|Jesé guarding the ball from [[Tiago Ilori]]. His ability to retain possession has led to comparisons with [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].]]
Jesé is able to play across the front line, operating either as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]], [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|second striker]] or [[Forward (association football)#Centre forward|centre-forward]], or in his favoured position out on the [[Midfielder#Winger|wing]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12040/8839181/la-liga-real-madrid-forward-jese-rodriguez-pens-new-four-year-deal|title=La Liga: Real Madrid forward Jese Rodriguez pens new four-year deal|website=Sky Sports|date=24 July 2013|access-date=26 December 2016|archive-date=20 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120213315/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/12040/8839181/la-liga-real-madrid-forward-jese-rodriguez-pens-new-four-year-deal|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://outsideoftheboot.com/2014/01/15/100-best-young-players-watch-2014-forwardswingers-20-11/|title=100 Best Young Players to watch out for in 2014: Forwards/Wingers ( 20–11 )|website=Outside of the Boot|date=15 January 2014|access-date=3 January 2017|archive-date=26 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226141840/http://outsideoftheboot.com/2014/01/15/100-best-young-players-watch-2014-forwardswingers-20-11|url-status=live}}</ref> During his time at the Castilla, Jesé was often deployed in a [[Deep-lying forward|false 9]] role in the team's 4–3–3 formation, and regularly switched flanks due to his ability to use both feet.<ref name="False9">{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1636590/real-madrid-jese-world-class-toril-says?cc=5739|title=Jese Rodriguez tipped for the top|website=ESPN|date=3 December 2013|access-date=7 December 2013|archive-date=31 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231220043/http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1636590/real-madrid-jese-world-class-toril-says?cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2145065/la-liga-jese-rodriguezs-return-boosts-an-already-lethal-real-madrid-attack|title=Jese Rodriguez's return boosts an already lethal Real Madrid attack|website=ESPN|last=Rigg|first=Nicholas|date=13 November 2014|access-date=2 January 2017|archive-date=3 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103094851/http://www.espnfc.com/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2145065/la-liga-jese-rodriguezs-return-boosts-an-already-lethal-real-madrid-attack|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2013, in his role as the club's sporting director at the time, Zinedine Zidane declared himself an admirer of Jesé's direct style of football and goal scoring ability.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/06/03/en/football/real_madrid/1370248035.html|title=Zidane backs Jesé for first team|website=Marca|last=Jimenez|first=Ruben|date=6 March 2013|access-date=26 December 2016|archive-date=19 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819234334/http://www.marca.com/2013/06/03/en/football/real_madrid/1370248035.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Following Jesé's promotion to Real Madrid's first team in 2013, manager Carlo Ancelotti played him in a winger position, where he could cut inside from the wing both with the ball and without, to create chances and score goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1628751/angel-di-maria-jese-rodriguez-stand-cristiano-ronaldo-real-madrid-galatasaray?cc=5739|title=Di Maria or Jese set to face Galatasaray|last=Corrigan|first=Dermot|website=ESPN|date=26 November 2013|access-date=19 December 2013|archive-date=1 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101072837/http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1628751/angel-di-maria-jese-rodriguez-stand-cristiano-ronaldo-real-madrid-galatasaray?cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref> His progression with Real Madrid's senior side often saw him compared to teammate Cristiano Ronaldo due to the similarities in their style as well as Jesé's technical ability, close control, pace and dribbling abilities. Jesé welcomed the comparison to Ronaldo and in a 2013 interview with ''Marca'' named the [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese]] as his favourite player, ahead of [[Brazil national football team|Brazilian]] namesake, [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]], and [[Ronaldinho]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://outsideoftheboot.com/2014/10/02/scout-report-jese-rodriguez-real-madrid-spains-young-superstar/|title=Scout Report: Jese Rodriguez: Real Madrid & Spain's young superstar|website=Outside of the Boot Football|last=Saric|first=Miran|date=2 October 2014|access-date=26 December 2016|archive-date=11 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811010305/http://outsideoftheboot.com/2014/10/02/scout-report-jese-rodriguez-real-madrid-spains-young-superstar/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spanish-football/2013/06/18/4056843/jese-flattered-by-cristiano-ronaldo-comparisons|title=Jese flattered by Cristiano Ronaldo comparisons|website=Goal|last=Coerts|first=Stefan|date=18 June 2013|access-date=26 December 2016|archive-date=27 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227061107/http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spanish-football/2013/06/18/4056843/jese-flattered-by-cristiano-ronaldo-comparisons|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jesé was born to Pascual Rodríguez, a pharmacy worker, and María Ruiz. When he joined Real Madrid at the age of 14, he made a promise to his father that he would help him retire by pursuing a career in football. The day after he signed his first professional contract with Real Madrid, Jesé's father was able to retire from the pharmacy at which he worked. He has the names of his parents tattooed on the back of his hands and in 2014 bought them a house in [[Gran Canaria]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/12/24/en/football/real_madrid/1387841445.html|title="Jesé will be a world class player"|website=Marca|last=Cerezo|first=Hugo|date=24 December 2013|access-date=26 December 2016|archive-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818093420/http://www.marca.com/2013/12/24/en/football/real_madrid/1387841445.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Jesé has four sons, Jesé Jr. (born 2012), Neizan (born 2016), Nyan (born 2017), Kenai (born 2019) and one daughter, Aylén (2020).<ref>{{cite web|title=Stoke City boss backing Jese to brave baby anguish|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stoke-city-boss-backing-jese-483795|website=Stoke Sentinel|date=15 September 2017|access-date=16 September 2017|archive-date=16 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916225348/http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stoke-city-boss-backing-jese-483795|url-status=live}}</ref> He learned of the birth of his second son over social media platform [[Instagram]] after the mother of the child claimed that he was the father in a post in November 2016. A [[Genealogical DNA test|DNA test]] was conducted soon after which confirmed Jesé to be the father.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadridnews.com/jese-rodriguez-son-father-7226|title=Jese Rodriguez, a model son and father|publisher=Real Madrid News|last=Martinez|first=Laura|date=3 March 2014|access-date=12 March 2014|archive-date=12 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312225302/http://www.realmadridnews.com/jese-rodriguez-son-father-7226|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vanitatis.elconfidencial.com/noticias/2016-12-15/jese-rodriguez-melody-santana-paternidad-adn-psg-nino-instagram_1303959/|title=El ADN confirma que el futbolista Jesé es el padre del hijo que conoció por Instagram|website=Vanitatis|last=Bolonio|first=Marta|date=15 December 2016|language=es|access-date=20 July 2017|archive-date=4 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804113648/http://www.vanitatis.elconfidencial.com/noticias/2016-12-15/jese-rodriguez-melody-santana-paternidad-adn-psg-nino-instagram_1303959/|url-status=live}}</ref> Jesé's third son, Nyan was born prematurely in 2017 and suffered from a number of medical conditions from birth. The following year, he went through a public and acrimonious breakup with Nyan's mother, Aurah Ruiz, which culminated in Ruiz taking Jesé to court where she accused him of neglecting his duties as a father.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.es/estilo/gente/abci-aurah-ruiz-estalla-jese-rodriguez-miami-ahorrate-comida-y-pagale-medico-hijo-nyan-201806060121_noticia.html|title=Aurah Ruiz estalla al ver a Jesé Rodríguez en Miami: "Ahórrate una comida y págale el médico a tu hijo Nyan"|publisher=ABC|date=6 June 2018|language=es|access-date=2 August 2018|archive-date=2 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802164110/https://www.abc.es/estilo/gente/abci-aurah-ruiz-estalla-jese-rodriguez-miami-ahorrate-comida-y-pagale-medico-hijo-nyan-201806060121_noticia.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/vaya-mundo/20180728/451147639374/sigue-la-guerra-entre-jese-y-aurah-ruiz.html|title=Sigue la guerra entre Jesé y Aurah Ruiz|publisher=Mundo Deportivo|date=28 July 2018|language=es|access-date=2 August 2018|archive-date=2 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802162700/https://www.mundodeportivo.com/vaya-mundo/20180728/451147639374/sigue-la-guerra-entre-jese-y-aurah-ruiz.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He responded with a counter-suit against Ruiz for slander in which he allegedly asked that she pay "one Euro and be sentenced to three to five years in prison."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/vaya-mundo/20190417/461708471116/aurah-ruiz-jese-rodriguez-quiere-que-vaya-a-la-carcel.html|title=Aurah Ruiz: 'Jesé Rodríguez quiere que vaya a la cárcel'|publisher=Mundo Deportivo|date=17 April 2019|language=es|access-date=19 April 2019|archive-date=19 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190419203321/https://www.mundodeportivo.com/vaya-mundo/20190417/461708471116/aurah-ruiz-jese-rodriguez-quiere-que-vaya-a-la-carcel.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2014, just a week after suffering a cruciate ligament injury with Real Madrid, Jesé had to be rescued when a suspected gas explosion set fire to the luxury apartment block in which he was staying at the time.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.sportsmole.co.uk/off-the-pitch/real-madrid/news/fire-brigade-called-to-jeses-apartment_146488.html |title=Fire brigade called to Jese's apartment |date=26 March 2014 |access-date=5 April 2020 |archive-date=29 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140329122905/http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/off-the-pitch/real-madrid/news/fire-brigade-called-to-jeses-apartment_146488.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Aside from football, Jesé is also a musician and formed a Spanish [[reggaeton]] band called Big Flow with close friend DJ Nuno in March 2014. Together, the pair released two singles on [[YouTube]], the first of which was titled La Mano Arriba. In November the same year, the group disbanded with Jesé announcing he would be pursuing a solo career in 2015 under the name 'Jey M.'<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/138240/jese-not-your-average-footballer/|title=Jesé – Not Your Average Footballer|website=Inside Spanish Football|last=Wilde|first=Tom|date=3 December 2014|access-date=2 January 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170103165449/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/138240/jese-not-your-average-footballer/|archive-date=3 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadridnews.com/jese-unveils-reggaeton-music-band-big-flow-7756|title=Jese Rodriguez unveils reggaeton music band Big Flow|website=Real Madrid News|last=Martinez|first=Laura|date=18 March 2014|access-date=20 July 2017|archive-date=16 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816235225/http://www.realmadridnews.com/jese-unveils-reggaeton-music-band-big-flow-7756|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Jesé inicia su carrera musical en solitario como 'Jey M'|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20141127/real-madrid/jese-inicia-su-carrera-musical-en-solitario-como-jey-m_54420825256.html|website=Mundo Deportivo|last=Zarate|first=Oscar|date=27 November 2014|language=es|access-date=20 July 2017|archive-date=16 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816235436/http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20141127/real-madrid/jese-inicia-su-carrera-musical-en-solitario-como-jey-m_54420825256.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2018, he released a single titled ''La Prueba'' – The Proof - from which he sought to donate proceeds for research towards diseases such [[congenital hyperinsulinism]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jese-stoke-jeym-reggaeton-batman-1637434|title=Stoke City disaster Jese's new song: 'I want to put my batmobile in your batcave'|work=Stoke Sentinel|last=Smith|first=Peter|date=4 June 2018|access-date=4 June 2018|archive-date=30 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930033536/https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jese-stoke-jeym-reggaeton-batman-1637434|url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2020, Jesé ended his contract early with Paris Saint-Germain. He had reportedly broken [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] regulations while being on a trip to the [[Canary Islands]], and was involved in a sex scandal having supposedly cheated on his partner with her friend Rocio Amar earlier in the year. Both events contributed to PSG terminating his contract.<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 December 2020|title=PSG sack Jese Rodriguez following sex scandal and breaking Covid rules by partying in Canary Islands|url=https://www.caughtoffside.com/2020/12/06/psg-sack-jese-rodriguez-following-sex-scandal-and-breaking-covid-rules-by-partying-in-canary-islands/|website=Caught Offside|access-date=6 December 2020|archive-date=6 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201206134219/https://www.caughtoffside.com/2020/12/06/psg-sack-jese-rodriguez-following-sex-scandal-and-breaking-covid-rules-by-partying-in-canary-islands/|url-status=live}}</ref>
